meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1/1F, Thursday 16 May 2024, P76922A), downloaded from qualifications.pearson.com. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Third Edexcel series in the audit. Extraction was clean: all 28 (Total for Question) lines recovered and summing to the printed 80, so no part total had to be inferred. Coded WITH mark_split.

coding_notes: q3 (name the type of angle marked y) tagged angles_on_lines_and_circles, the documented handling for classifying an angle — there is no node of its own and measuring_lines_and_angles is about protractor use.
q5 and q11b (a square root and a power of 2) tagged indices, the documented handling for roots as well as powers. q18 is the same node: the answer is 1, from a zero index.
q13b tagged calculating_simple_probability then ratio: the answer is a probability, but the mark scheme's process mark is for establishing the 2 : 1 split of coin counts from an equal split of value.

q21b tagged irregular_and_improper_fractions first. The question is set as a division, but the mistake the mark scheme wants identified is purely in converting 35/24 to a mixed number — it explicitly refuses 'he should have done keep, flip, change'.
q22b tagged proportion alone, not areas_of_compound_shapes: the area is settled by part (a) and the only thing (b) tests is what a larger coverage rate does to the conclusion.
q26 tagged ratio before fractions_of_amounts — four of the five marks chain two ratios together, and the fraction of the total is one step of the four.
